item.title: Lindsay Clancy’s Murder Trial Ended With a Hung Jury. What Now?
item.description: Ms. Clancy still faces murder charges for killing her three children. She is likely to remain in a hospital, and prosecutors may decide to retry her.
item.dc:creator: Jacey Fortin, Maia Spoto and Jenna Russell
item.media:description: Kevin Reddington, Ms. Clancy’s lawyer, said that he expected the district attorney to try her for first-degree murder again.

item.title: A More Confident Iran Emerges After Six Months of War With the U.S.
item.description: New intelligence reports have assessed that Iran now has a far better understanding of its capabilities and the limits of U.S. power.
item.dc:creator: Julian E. Barnes and Dustin Volz
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Emile Ducke for The New York Times
item.media:description: A crowd mourning Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed at the start of the war. U.S. intelligence reports, some current and former officials said, suggest that any agreement to fully end the war will be hard to reach.

item.title: Yemen’s Houthis Push Toward Red Sea Strait as Ground Fighting Escalates
item.description: The Houthis, an Iran-backed militia, appear to be trying to gain control of a port city near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a key choke point for global trade.
item.dc:creator: Shuaib Almosawa and Saeed Al-Batati
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Houthi supporters at a rally marking the Prophet Muhammad’s birthday, known as Moulid, in Sanaa, Yemen’s capital, in August.

item.title: Israel Says It Is Cementing Its Foothold in Southern Lebanon
item.description: The recent capture of a strategic ridge has further entrenched the Israeli occupation of Lebanese territory, as efforts to broker lasting peace have floundered.
item.dc:creator: Euan Ward and David M. Halbfinger
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: In a screen grab obtained from a social media video released on Aug. 22, smoke rose following strikes on Ali al-Taher ridge in Nabatieh, Lebanon.

item.title: Robust Hiring Reinforces Strength of the U.S. Economy
item.description: Employers added 162,000 jobs and unemployment held at 4.1 percent last month, signs of a stability that contrasted with high inflation weighing on households and markets.
item.dc:creator: Sydney Ember
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)

item.title: Trump Threatens to Halt Some Trade Unless the Fed Cuts Rates
item.description: The president said he could halt trade between the United States and countries with which it has a trade deficit if the central bank doesn’t do his bidding.
item.dc:creator: Tony Romm and Colby Smith
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: President Trump’s remarks were his latest attempt to pressure the Federal Reserve into lowering interest rates.

item.title: Supreme Court Sides With Republicans in TV Ad Fight
item.description: Republican groups had asked the court to clear the way for political parties to pay the same low-cost ad rates as candidates, a move that could undercut a Democratic advantage in the midterms.
item.dc:creator: Abbie VanSickle
item.media:description: National Republican groups had filed an emergency application to the Supreme Court asking the justices to step in and clear the way for them to get the lower TV ad rates.

item.title: Homeland Security Dept. Asks for Inquiries Into Voting Machines
item.description: Critics of ballot-marking devices have claimed that hackers could manipulate digital codes on ballots. Election experts say the systems are safe to use.
item.dc:creator: Alan Feuer, Nick Corasaniti and Alexandra Berzon
item.media:credit: Chase Castor for The New York Times
item.media:description: Voters used electronic ballots at a polling location in Kansas in August.

item.title: Trump Administration Issues Subpoenas For Voter Data in Nevada
item.description: The request comes as the government has escalated efforts to prove President Trump’s false claims of widespread voter fraud.
item.dc:creator: Nick Corasaniti and Alan Feuer
item.media:credit: Bridget Bennett for The New York Times
item.media:description: In December, the Justice Department sued Nevada and 29 other states, demanding that they hand over private, unredacted voter files.

item.title: Sandra Bullock, Nicole Kidman and the Other ‘Practical Magic 2’ Stars on the Unlikely Sequel
item.description: Sandra Bullock, Nicole Kidman, Joey King and Maisie Williams on the unlikely sequel, embracing their witchiness and their hopes for a third film.
item.dc:creator: Ashley Spencer

item.title: Pentagon Agreement With N.I.H. on Biodefense Draws Alarm From Democrats
item.description: Under a new partnership, the Defense Department would play a larger role in biodefense and pandemic preparedness. Democrats warned it could allow a Pentagon cash grab.
item.dc:creator: Catie Edmondson and Carolyn Y. Johnson
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases
item.media:description: The agreement, a copy of which was obtained by The New York Times, is focused on chemical and biological defense research.

item.title: RFK Jr. Hires Army Doctor Who Opposed Covid Shots to Investigate if They Killed 2,500 Troops
item.description: In a legal deposition, the doctor, Theresa Long, compared immunizing service members against Covid to Nazi doctors experimenting on concentration camp prisoners.
item.dc:creator: Apoorva Mandavilli and Jan Hoffman
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:credit: Kenny Holston for The New York Times

item.title: Corporate America Is Getting Hooked on Open-Source A.I.

item.title: The Risk of Russian Sabotage in Europe: A Fight That Spirals Out of Control
item.description: Europe’s options are limited in responding to an unnerving series of plots and provocations. But the odds of unpredictable consequences are rising.
item.dc:creator: Michael Schwirtz and Adam Goldman
item.media:description: President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia has long viewed his country as being in conflict with the West, but he has denied Russia’s involvement in European sabotage.

item.title: Kushner and Witkoff to Go to Russia and Ukraine to Revive Peace Talks

item.dc:creator: David E. Sanger

item.title: Russian Drone Strikes Office of Ukraine’s Intelligence Chief
item.description: The attack came as the American envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were said to be planning imminent visits to Kyiv and to Moscow.

item.media:description: The headquarters of Ukraine’s security service in Kyiv after a Russian drone strike on Friday. The building is just across the street from the landmark St. Sophia Cathedral.
